course_name_original: Teoría de Estructuras y Construcciones Industriales
course_name_en: Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions
prerequisites: Having completed the subjects corresponding to the BASIC TRAINING modules and those corresponding to the second year of the COMMON TO THE INDUSTRIAL BRANCH module.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop industrial engineering projects aimed at the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Knowledge and use of the principles of material resistance.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Knowledge and skills to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and material resistance to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Choose the ideal location for the industrial plant.
Carry out studies of implementation and organization of the industrial plant.
Evaluate the environmental impact of industrial constructions.
Statically calculate bar structures.
Choose the most used structural typologies and the most appropriate modeling for their analysis.

syllabus_topics: Calculation of isostatic structures with rigid and articulated joints (Trusses)
Calculation of hyperstatic structures with rigid and articulated joints (Force method and Slope-deflection method)
The industrial building: design and structural behavior
Calculation bases and actions on the industrial building

assessment_methods.method: Theory of Structures Final Presential Exam (Continuous Assessment option)
Theory of Structures Intermediate Tests (Continuous Assessment option)
Theory of Structures Final Presential Exam (No Continuous Assessment option)
Theory of Structures Practical Knowledge Test (No Continuous Assessment option)
Theory of Structures Final Presential Exam (Differentiated Assessment / Extraordinary Calls)
Theory of Structures Practical Knowledge Test (Differentiated Assessment / Extraordinary Calls)
Industrial Constructions Submitted Tasks and Laboratory Practices
Industrial Constructions Final Presential Exam (Differentiated Assessment)

assessment_rules: The final grade for the course will be calculated as the average of the grades for its two parts (Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions), requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 points in each. For Theory of Structures, in the ordinary call, students can choose between continuous assessment (80% final exam + 20% intermediate tests) or no continuous assessment (90% final exam + 10% practical knowledge test). A minimum of 2 points out of 10 is required in each important topic (PTV, isostatic and hyperstatic structures). For Industrial Constructions, the final written exam has a weight of 75% (minimum 4/10) and submitted tasks and laboratory practices 25% (laboratory practice attendance is mandatory and a minimum of 5/10 is required). In extraordinary calls and differentiated assessment, specific rules apply, which may include a 100% final exam covering theory and practical aspects.
